essence: Fractal Noise procedurally generates a continuous grayscale field by combining noise detail across multiple scales, then maps that field through contrast, brightness, and overflow handling before compositing it over the layer. Scale determines the size of the generated forms; Complexity and Sub controls add progressively smaller structure; Offset Turbulence or Evolution changes which part/state of the field is sampled, creating motion without moving source pixels. Use its grayscale output directly as clouds, smoke, grain, or texture, or as a matte/displacement-driving layer.
manifests_as: A monochrome, endlessly variable field that can read as soft clouds, smoky turbulence, coarse grain, liquid blobs, or dense organic texture depending primarily on scale and detail settings.

key_levers.name: Fractal Type
key_levers.effect: Selects the underlying fractal algorithm, changing the character of the generated structures before scale, contrast, and animation are applied.

key_levers.name: Contrast
key_levers.effect: Separates light and dark regions: increasing it makes the field more mask-like and graphic, while reducing it leaves softer gray transitions.

key_levers.name: Brightness
key_levers.effect: Shifts the entire generated field lighter or darker, controlling how much of it reads as white versus black after contrast.

key_levers.name: Scale
key_levers.effect: Sets the overall spatial size of noise features: higher values produce fewer, larger clouds/blobs; lower values produce finer texture and grain.

key_levers.name: Complexity
key_levers.effect: Adds more layers of progressively smaller noise detail; raise it for richer turbulent structure, lower it for simpler broad forms.

key_levers.name: Sub Influence (%)
key_levers.effect: Controls how strongly the smaller sub-noise layer modifies the main pattern; higher values make fine structure more visible and disruptive.

key_levers.name: Offset Turbulence
key_levers.effect: Pans the sampling position through the procedural field, creating directional drifting motion while preserving the noise's internal scale and contrast.

key_levers.name: Evolution
key_levers.effect: Generates new states of the fractal over time rather than merely panning it; animate it for boiling, morphing, or churning texture.

key_levers.name: Opacity
key_levers.effect: Controls the visibility of the effect result in its selected blend mode without changing the underlying noise pattern.

config_recipes.soft drifting clouds: Fractal Type=1; Contrast=120; Brightness=5; Scale=220%; Complexity=5; Sub Influence (%)=45%; animate Offset Turbulence slowly from [320,180] to [500,220].
config_recipes.dense smoky turbulence: Fractal Type=1; Contrast=180; Brightness=-10; Scale=140%; Complexity=8; Sub Influence (%)=75%; animate Evolution at roughly 35 degrees per second.
config_recipes.fine film-grain-like breakup: Fractal Type=1; Contrast=60; Brightness=0; Scale=18%; Complexity=2; Sub Influence (%)=20%; animate Evolution rapidly; reduce Opacity to 10-25%.
config_recipes.high-contrast animated matte: Fractal Type=1; Contrast=350; Brightness=-20; Scale=170%; Complexity=4; Sub Influence (%)=55%; animate Evolution at roughly 20 degrees per second.

reasoning_hooks: Scale is the primary read-size control: set it before judging Complexity, because detail that looks excessive at one scale may disappear at another.
Offset Turbulence produces travel through a fixed field; Evolution changes the field itself. Use offset for wind/drift and evolution for boiling or morphing.
Contrast and Brightness act on the generated grayscale values, so establish the texture structure first, then use them to set matte coverage or black/white separation.
Uniform Scaling is enabled by default; Scale Width and Scale Height will not create independent stretching until Uniform Scaling is disabled.
A static Fractal Noise layer can look like a still texture rather than an effect; animate Offset Turbulence or Evolution when the request implies living smoke, water, energy, or grain.
Very high Complexity and Sub Influence can add expensive fine detail without improving a small or blurred final image; judge at delivery resolution.
